lines: Odlum Brown's $28B+ AUM base as of May 2026 represents an 87% increase from the $15B reported in 2020, translating to an approximately 11% compound annual growth rate — achieved entirely through organic advisor-led growth with no merger or acquisition activity confirmed.  [E-001,E-002,E-088] This growth trajectory places OB firmly in the top tier of BC-based independent wealth managers by AUM. The firm's 2022 Client Insights survey (conducted by an external facilitator) showed 96% client satisfaction and 97% advisor satisfaction — the operational base underpinning this growth.  [E-010] A 56-fold increase in the Odlum Brown Model Portfolio since its 1994 inception (managed by CIO Murray Leith) provides the long-term performance credibility that sustains client retention and new asset inflows.
Classification: ACCELERATING | 6-Year CAGR: ~11.0% | Growth model: 100% organic (no M&A confirmed)

Odlum Brown's 87% organic AUM growth over six years — from $15B in 2020 to $28B+ in 2026 — at an 11% compound annual rate is among the strongest organic growth trajectories for an independent dealer in Canada. This growth has been achieved without any merger or acquisition activity, exclusively through advisor-led client acquisition and retention. The consistency of this growth through periods of significant market volatility (COVID-19 2020, inflation shock 2022, rate cycle 2022–2024) demonstrates structural resilience and deep client trust.  [E-001,E-088,E-116,E-117] From a Salesforce Account Executive perspective, this trajectory confirms two things: first, that budget availability is strong and expanding; and second, that the constraint on further growth is now technology — the BRC data showing declining CRM scores is the single data point in an otherwise accelerating growth story.

Wellington-Altus leads 21 of 27 BRC categories and represents OB's primary competitive threat — it outperforms OB materially on (digital channels, 4.5 vs. 1.98) and (marketing, 4.0 vs. 1.49), the two categories with the largest peer gaps. Nicola Wealth, with $17.1B AUM — smaller than OB's $28B — deploys Salesforce, Marketo, Tableau, and RPA — a more advanced marketing and data technology stack than OB. Leith Wheeler and Mawer represent the traditional independent dealer posture that OB risks sliding toward if the Wellington-Altus technology gap is not addressed.
OB leads all peers on Cybersecurity (4.05) and Compliance (3.98) — both confirmed by T1 evidence. These are genuine competitive strengths, not scoring artefacts.
